facts.summary: Ermita de planta centrada diseñada por Torcuato Cayón de la Vega (1772-1774) sobre un antiguo molino, en la Colina de Santa Ana. Pórtico octogonal de ocho lados iguales con tres arcos de medio punto por lado sobre pilastras (el central mayor); cúpula hemisférica sobre tambor con cuatro óculos, remate con veleta. Escalera ancha en el frente principal. Paredes encaladas con bandas amarillo ocre, puerta negra, rejas bajas de forja entre arcos, plaza empedrada con estatua blanca sobre pedestal blanco-amarillo, palmeras y pinos.

places.name: Convento e Iglesia de Jesús Nazareno
places.catastro: footprint = OSM way 150927356 (4 vertices, 22.5 x 14.5 m, 302 m2); match Catastro building by point-in-polygon at centroid x -3907.2 z -1921.6
places.description: Baroque convent church of the Agustinas Recoletas (founded 1666 by Madre Antonia de Jesús, built 1667-1674). Single rectangular nave ('de cajón') with side chapels between buttresses, flat head, Latin cross inscribed, barrel vaults, dome on pendentives. Its glory is the white Genoese-marble baroque side portal with four Solomonic columns facing the pedestrian Plaza/Calle de Jesús Nazareno, and a four-stage white corner bell tower with yellow cornices. Whitewashed walls with yellow (albero/ochre) bands.

facts.fact: Convent founded 1666, church built 1667-1674, baroque; cloistered Agustinas Recoletas

Single nave church with side chapels, tower in the outer corner chapel; ground floor of tower holds an open chapel with a large round-arched window facing the plaza (seen: barred arched window at tower foot, left of portal)
facts.source: Wikipedia + Commons photo Iglesia Jesús Nazareno 00/03

facts.fact: Portal: white Genoese marble, four Solomonic (twisted) columns with Corinthian capitals on tall carved pedestals, lintelled central opening, marble statue of Jesús Nazareno in a niche above under a broken pediment with garlands, vases and cherubs; statues of saints in side niches; small oculi in the pediment wings
Door: double-leaf, very dark brown panelled wood, about 3 m wide and 4.5 m high, set within the marble frame

Walls whitewashed with horizontal yellow (ochre) bands/cornices at roof eaves, mid-height and plinth line of the tower; flat panelled recesses on the wall; several round oculi (about 0.6 m) under the eaves line
Roof: red clay Arab tiles on the nave, eave bordered by yellow band

Tower: four stages separated by thin yellow cornices; two central stages almost blind, top stage with round-arched openings on four sides holding bells, framed by yellow pilasters; wiki says capped with a polychrome ceramic dome; photo shows a low top with plants

Plaza de Jesús Nazareno / Calle Jesús Nazareno is pedestrian paved, directly north of the church (OSM way 53620041/427627827 at z≈-1934, bearing east-west); a flower pot (red begonias) stands at the portal foot
Orientation: viewing the portal from the plaza the tower is at the LEFT corner, so with the facade on the north edge the tower sits at the NE corner of the footprint
A glazed tile (azulejo) plaque of the Virgen (blue ground, red robe, gold) exists on a wall in the area (jn_01)
facts.source: Commons Chiclana de la Frontera - Iglesia Convento de Nuestro Padre Jesús Nazareno 01

places.notes: Heights and tower position are estimates. Wikipedia 'cúpula de cerámica policromada' not clearly visible on the photo.

places.name: Iglesia de San Telmo (Santísima Trinidad)
places.catastro: OSM footprint 4 vertices 44 x 14.7 m, 649 m2; match Catastro building by centroid x -3870.9 z -2186.5
places.description: 18th-century church (parish moved here 1778; built 1783 per municipal tourism) of the sea-going devotion to San Pedro Telmo, shrine of the Virgen de los Remedios (patron of Chiclana). Austere exterior: whitewashed street front with an arched nailed door, ochre/cream cornice bands, a single-gable pediment with a round oculus and an angular espadaña (bell gable) at one corner. Latin-cross plan inside with barrel vaults and lunettes.

facts.fact: Built 1783 (tourism office) on an older hermitage; parish moved from San Martín church in 1778; known as Santuario de Ntra. Sra. de las Angustias y San Pedro Telmo

Facade: whitewashed, ~15 m wide; ground floor has a semicircular-arched double door in dark brown/black studded wood (~2.6 m wide, ~4.2 m tall) set in a plastered arch recess; dark grey plinth ~1 m high running along the whole facade
facts.source: Commons Iglesia San Telmo Chiclana.jpg / Portada San Telmo Chiclana.jpg

facts.fact: A pale ochre/cream moulded cornice band runs horizontally at about 5 m height across the facade and continues along eaves as raking cornice around a triangular gable (pediment) with a round oculus framed in the same colour
Upper level: one rectangular window with white surround and brown wooden frame (6 panes) above the door, plus small black wrought-iron balconies with narrow doors left, and an apartment balcony right
Espadaña (bell gable): at the left corner of the facade, one arched opening with a bell, cream-ochre scrolled framing, small iron balcony at its foot, topped with a stork nest
Glazed tile panel of the Virgen de los Remedios (blue/gold frame, ~0.9 x 1.2 m) with small lantern, above right of the door at ~3 m; commemorative marble plaques left of the door (two, ~0.6 m wide)

Paving in front: grey cobble/sett paving with small square and rectangular setts plus iron drain covers; two potted lollipop (bitter orange / ficus-like) trees in dark grey square planters with pink flowers; black cast-iron two-arm street lamp (~4.5 m) at the right

Street adjacency: Calle Fraile runs along the short west edge (OSM 53620048), Calle Nuestra Señora de los Remedios along the NW long wall (OSM 142716092, pedestrian), Calle de la Plaza pedestrian to the north

Which short edge carries the facade: edge A-B (SW short edge, 14.6 m) runs exactly along Calle Fraile so the facade is assumed there, outward normal bearing ~316 (NW); the bell gable on the left corner viewed from the street = near vertex B

places.notes: Dome (Cúpula San Telmo.jpg) not inspected. Roof/side wall heights guessed.
